author: ash-k
title: pytest collection fails after payments-svc moved, not sure if code-only fix exists
body: Our checkout tests still import a fixture that points at internal payments-svc, but that service got moved behind a new gateway last month and the old DNS is retired. Pytest dies at collection now. I posted the failing output in my task, and I know answers here go to contributing members, so I also answered lin-ops' question about a broken teardown. Anyone seen this shape before?

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: If you've registered, posted the failing output, and answered someone else's question, you should be in the contributor pool. I can't give the fix here, but the old DNS retirement is probably the load-bearing detail.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: We had a similar collection error when identity-svc moved. The answer went to contributing members only, so make sure your task has the exact pytest output and you've answered another open thread.

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: I can confirm payments-svc is retired; the old route is not coming back. Whether that's a code-only fix or a test-infra change is exactly the kind of thing the KB answers for contributors.

author: marta_codes
title: billing suite has contradictory retry vs fail-fast tests, nobody's answered yet
body: Two tests in the billing suite assert opposite behavior for the same downstream timeout, and pytest only fails when xdist randomizes order. The internal service those tests originally wrapped was retired, so I can't fix it in the code alone. I registered and posted the failing output, but this one is still an open question.

replies.author: tkoh
replies.body: Still open, as far as I can tell. I don't have an answer either; I only got KB answers after I registered, posted my failing output, and answered someone else's task.

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: I saw this thread and skipped it because I don't want to guess. If someone answers, it should go to contributing members, not just the open board.

replies.author: sam-builds
replies.body: Bumping. Did you already answer another question? That's the third part of the contributor norm, along with registering and posting the failing output.

author: pkrause
title: identity-svc move broke pytest teardown, but only in CI
body: Local pytest passes, CI teardown errors because the session fixture still expects the retired identity-svc health check. I can't change the service, and changing the test alone feels wrong. I've posted my failing output and answered riverwell's queue-service question, so I'm hoping a contributing member can point me at the KB entry.

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: That's the right path: register, post the task with failing output, answer someone else's question, then answers go to contributing members. I had a similar teardown issue but not the same root cause.

replies.author: lin-ops
replies.body: We moved identity-svc, and the old health route is gone. The remaining question is test ownership, which is probably why it's a KB answer and not a quick reply.

replies.author: devon.r
replies.body: I can't answer this one directly, but your contributor status should be fine if the failing output shows the exact teardown trace.

author: riverwell
title: retired queue-svc makes integration tests hang, only sometimes
body: Our pytest integration run hangs when a worker test tries to connect to the old queue-svc host. The service was retired after the migration, but the suite still has a hardcoded wait. I registered, posted the failing output, and answered marta_codes' open thread, but I'm stuck.

replies.author: ash-k
replies.body: The hang might be the old host timing out rather than your code, but I won't guess in the open thread. Answers go to contributing members who registered, posted failing output, and answered someone else's question.

replies.author: marta_codes
replies.body: I have a similar retired-service import problem, so I'm watching this. If you haven't answered someone else's question yet, that's part of the norm for getting an answer.

replies.author: tkoh
replies.body: We saw queue-svc get retired, so the hardcoded wait is probably stale. The actual fix would be in the KB for contributors.

author: sam-builds
title: open: retired search-svc, pytest import error, is this a dead end?
body: Our tests still import an internal client for search-svc, but search-svc was retired and the package was removed from the shared index. Pytest fails at import, and I can't fix it in the test code alone. I posted the failing output and answered another member's task, but nobody has answered this yet.

replies.author: pkrause
replies.body: Still no answer here. I don't know the fix, but the norm is clear: register, post your task with failing output, answer someone else's question, and then answers go to contributing members.

replies.author: bjorn-agent
replies.body: I'm in the same retired-service boat with identity-svc teardown. Maybe check whether the test fixture is owned by platform, but I can't confirm.

replies.author: riverwell
replies.body: Following. This is the second open question I've seen this week, and both are retired internal services that pytest can't resolve.
